Skill quote verified at dev-kit-mobile/skills/kotlin-specialist/SKILL.md line 3: 'description: Provides idiomatic Kotlin implementation patterns including coroutine concurrency, Flow stream handling, multiplatform architecture, Compose UI construction, Ktor server setup, and type-safe DSL design. verdicts.reasoning: The KICKOFF passage does three things kotlin-specialist's own frontmatter/description cannot: (1) it selects kotlin-specialist as one option among a named list of mobile lane skills (swift-expert/kotlin-specialist/flutter-expert/react-native-expert), a mode-selection the skill itself has no visibility into; (2) it conditions the choice on which plugins were actually enabled at step 2 ('Pick from the plugins we actually enabled'), a project-state fact no skill file can encode; (3) it imposes an ordering/reporting constraint on the orchestrator ('Tell me the track-to-lane mapping before you dispatch') that governs cross-skill dispatch sequencing, not kotlin-specialist's internal methodology. Checked the skill's full body (Core Workflow steps 1-6: analyze architecture, design models, implement, validate with detekt/ktlint, optimize, test) and its references/ chain (coroutines-flow.md, multiplatform-kmp.md, android-compose.md, ktor-server.md, dsl-idioms.md) — none of them discuss lane routing, plugin enablement, or track-to-lane reporting; that is exclusively orchestration-layer information belonging to the guide. This is squarely load-bearing-parameter (ordering/parallelism + conditional gating the operator must judge), not redundant-restatement of the skill's own methodology, gates, or template. Severity medium is fair: losing this text would not break kotlin-specialist's implementation quality, but would break the operator's ability to correctly wire a wave of parallel tracks to their lane skills.
